title: Commit Bodies and Footers — Explaining the Why
learning_objectives: Identify when a commit body is necessary vs. when the subject line is enough
Write a commit body that explains motivation and context, not implementation
Format commit bodies using the 72-character line wrap rule
Use commit footers to reference GitHub issues (Closes #N, Refs #N)
Write a complete, well-structured commit with subject, body, and footer
outline: When to write a body: complex changes, non-obvious decisions, breaking changes
What goes in a body: motivation, context, trade-offs — not what the diff shows
The 72-character wrap rule for body lines
Blank line separator: subject → blank line → body
Footer syntax: Closes #N, Fixes #N, Refs #N, BREAKING CHANGE:
Hands-on: Write one complete commit (subject + body + footer) for a Helm change

helm_context.feature: Documented design decisions in Helm commit history
helm_context.deliverable: One commit with a well-written body explaining a Helm architectural decision

criteria: Subject line meets 50-char rule and imperative mood (from L02)
Blank line correctly separates subject from body
Body explains motivation or context, not just what changed
Footer includes at least one issue reference using correct syntax

resources.title: How to Write a Git Commit Message (Chris Beams)

professor_constraints: Use Helm-specific examples — a design decision about data model, Google Calendar sync approach, etc.
Emphasize: 'explain why you made this choice, not what the code does'
Show a before/after: same change with only a subject vs. with a full body
Keep the hands-on exercise to one commit — quality over quantity
